stemBlocks.value: Solve x² + 6x + 1 = 0 by completing the square.
Think first: This will not factorise with whole numbers, so the completed square is the route to an exact surd answer.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p103-q13 from workbook page 103.

contentBlocks.value: half of 6 is 3, and 3² = 9, so x² + 6x = (x + 3)² − 9

solutionSteps.instruction: Take the square root of both sides, keeping both signs.
Subtract 3 from both sides and evaluate.

strategyBlocks.value: Rewrite the left side as a perfect square plus a constant, isolate the square, then take the square root of both sides remembering the ±.

whyThisWorks.value: Completing the square converts the equation into the form (something)² = number, and that form can be undone directly by a square root. The ± is essential because both a positive and a negative quantity square to the same value, which is why a quadratic has two roots. Leaving the answer as a surd keeps it exact; the decimals are only an approximation.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing only x + 3 = 2√2 and losing the second root.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing only x + 3 = 2√2 and losing the second root.
Avoid this: Simplifying √8 to 4 instead of 2√2.

commonErrors.misconception: Adding 9 to only one side of the equation when isolating the square.

examTip.value: Whenever you square-root both sides of an equation, write the ± immediately — it is the single most commonly dropped mark in this topic.
